title: Equivariant affine component charts and canonical generic germs
statement: Let $X,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme] with finite decompositions into disjoint open and closed integral subschemes $X_i$ ($i\in I$) and $Z_j$ ($j\in J$) [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Denote their generic points by $\eta_i,\xi_j$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Let $q:X\to Z$ be finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $\phi:I\to J$ satisfy $q(X_i)=Z_{\phi(i)}$ and $q(\eta_i)=\xi_{\phi(i)}$. Let a finite group $H$ act on $X$ by scheme automorphisms, permuting the $X_i$, with $q\circ h=q$ and $\phi(hi)=\phi(i)$. Fix $j\in J$ with $O=\phi^{-1}(j)\ne\varnothing$, and a nonempty affine open $V\subset Z_j$. Put $A=\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_Z)$, $W=q^{-1}V$, and $W_i=X_i\cap W$ for $i\in O$. Then $W$ and all $W_i$ are affine, every $W_i$ is nonempty and open and closed in $W$, and these $W_i$ cover $W$. The rings $A$ and $B_i=\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_X)$ are integral domains. The actual restriction map $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)\longrightarrow\prod_{i\in O}B_i$ is a ring isomorphism, equivariant for inverse pullback by $H$; thus $h$ induces $B_i\cong B_{hi}$. The composite $a_i:A\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)\to B_i$ is injective. Germs give canonical identifications $\kappa(\xi_j)=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $\kappa(\eta_i)=\operatorname{Frac}B_i$ [def-weil-residue-field], under which the residue-field map of $q$ is the unique fraction-field extension of $a_i$. If $D_i=\{h\in H:hi=i\}$, the inverse-pullback action of $D_i$ on $\kappa(\eta_i)$ is the extension of its action on $B_i$ to fractions. Here $\operatorname{Frac}R$ is the field of quotients $b/c$ with $b,c\in R$ and $c\ne0$, using the canonical injection of a domain $R$.

source.place: Tags 01I3 (lemma-standard-open-affine), 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), with algebra.tex Tag 00EE (lemma-disjoint-decomposition) and morphisms.tex Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions); agent equivariance and canonical-germ comparison.

proof.text: Since $Z_j$ is open in $Z$, the affine open $V\subset Z_j$ is also an affine open of $Z$. Finiteness of $q$ includes affineness, so $W=q^{-1}V$ is affine. If $x\in W\cap X_i$, then $q(x)\in Z_j\cap Z_{\phi(i)}$, hence $\phi(i)=j$. Conversely, for each $i\in O$, the generic point $\xi_j$ lies in the nonempty open $V$: otherwise the closed complement would contain the dense singleton $\{\xi_j\}$ and hence all of $Z_j$. Thus $\eta_i\in W_i$, since $q(\eta_i)=\xi_j$. Intersecting the given disjoint clopen decomposition of $X$ with $W$ proves that the nonempty $W_i$, $i\in O$, are pairwise disjoint, open and closed in $W$, and cover $W$.

source.place: Tag 01WH (definition-integral), definition of finite morphism; elementary inverse-image and generic-point argument

proof.text: Put $C=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_X)$ and use the affine identification $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}C$. For each $i\in O$, the clopen $W_i$ corresponds by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent] to $D(e_i)$ for an idempotent $e_i\in C$. Principal opens of affine schemes are affine by clause (b) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]; hence $W_i$ is affine. Both $V$ and $W_i$ are nonempty affine opens of the integral schemes $Z_j$ and $X_i$, respectively. Therefore $A$ and $B_i$ are domains by the definition of integral scheme.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-disjoint-union-product] to one $W_i$ and the union of the other components. Induction on the nonzero finite cardinality of $O$ identifies $C$ with $\prod_{i\in O}B_i$: for one component the map is the identity; removing one component gives the stated binary product isomorphism and the induction hypothesis on the remaining union. The resulting map has $i$th coordinate exactly restriction to $W_i$, so it is the actual map in the statement. In particular this construction chooses no abstract product identification.

source.place: Tag 01I5 (lemma-disjoint-union-affines), proof: product of section rings by the sheaf property; finite induction

proof.text:
For $h\in H$ one has $h(W)=W$ because $qh=q$, and $h(W_i)=W_{hi}$. Set $\rho_h=(h^{-1}|_W)^*:C\to C$ and $\beta_{h,i}=(h^{-1}|_{W_{hi}})^*:B_i\to B_{hi}$. These are ring isomorphisms, with inverse given by $h^*$ on the corresponding opens. Compatibility of the sheaf map of a scheme morphism with restrictions gives
$$\operatorname{res}_{hi}(\rho_h(s))=\beta_{h,i}(\operatorname{res}_i(s)).$$
Thus the product action is $(h\cdot b)_{hi}=\beta_{h,i}(b_i)$, and the isomorphism of step 3 is equivariant. Pullback reverses composition, so $\rho_{hk}=\rho_h\rho_k$ and $\beta_{hk,i}=\beta_{h,ki}\beta_{k,i}$; this verifies the left-action convention. Also $qh^{-1}=q$ gives $\beta_{h,i}a_i=a_{hi}$.

source.place: Tags 0091 (definition-ringed-space), 008J (definition-f-map), compatibility with restriction and composition; schemes.tex Tag 01HB (definition-locally-ringed-space); agent inverse-pullback calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] to $(Z_j,V,\xi_j)$ and to $(X_i,W_i,\eta_i)$. All its integrality, affine and nonemptiness hypotheses were checked above. It identifies $\mathcal O_{Z_j,\xi_j}$ and $\mathcal O_{X_i,\eta_i}$ as fields of fractions of $A$ and $B_i$, by the actual germ maps. Passing from an open subscheme to the ambient scheme does not change the stalk at one of its points: neighbourhoods contained in the open are cofinal, and restrictions give the inverse maps on germ representatives. Hence these are also $\mathcal O_{Z,\xi_j}$ and $\mathcal O_{X,\eta_i}$. A field has zero maximal ideal, so taking its residue field changes nothing. This gives the claimed canonical identifications $\kappa(\xi_j)=\operatorname{Frac}A$ and $\kappa(\eta_i)=\operatorname{Frac}B_i$.

source.place: Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), integral case; schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), generic stalk as localization at (0); Tag 01HB, residue field definition

proof.text:
Let $\lambda_i:\kappa(\xi_j)\to\kappa(\eta_i)$ be the residue-field map of $q$, and denote the injections supplied by step 5 by $\gamma_A$ and $\gamma_i$. Formula (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition], followed by restriction to $W_i$, gives
$$\lambda_i(\gamma_A(a))=\gamma_i(a_i(a))\qquad(a\in A).$$
The field homomorphism $\lambda_i$ is injective: its kernel is an ideal in a field and cannot contain $1$. If $a_i(a)=0$, the displayed formula implies $\lambda_i(\gamma_A(a))=0$, hence $a=0$. Thus $a_i$ is injective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift] to $\gamma_i\circ a_i$. Its unique extension agrees with $\lambda_i$ because both restrict to that map on $A$; explicitly
$$\lambda_i(a/c)=a_i(a)/a_i(c)\qquad(c\ne0).$$
This proves the comparison for the specified residue-field map, rather than for an unspecified field embedding.

source.place: Tag 008M (lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks) and preceding germ-representative construction; agent fraction-field formula and injectivity argument

proof.text:
If $h\in D_i$, the automorphism $h$ restricts to $W_i$ and fixes its generic point: the homeomorphism carries the dense singleton $\{\eta_i\}$ to a dense singleton in $X_i$, and the closed irreducible set $X_i$ has exactly one generic point by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. Let $\sigma_h$ be inverse pullback on $\kappa(\eta_i)$. The same germ identity (a) of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-stalk-map-composition], now for $h^{-1}$, gives $\sigma_h(\gamma_i(b))=\gamma_i(\beta_{h,i}(b))$ for every $b\in B_i$. Every element of the field is $b/c$ with $c\ne0$ by step 5, so
$$\sigma_h(b/c)=\beta_{h,i}(b)/\beta_{h,i}(c).$$
The denominator is nonzero since $\beta_{h,i}$ is an isomorphism. This is exactly the unique extension of $\beta_{h,i}$ to fractions, by [lem-weil-pbc-fraction-field-lift]. Stalk-map composition, formula (b), ensures these are the inverse-pullback group actions used in step 4.

source.place: Tag 008M (lemma-compose-f-maps-stalks), germ compatibility and composition; agent substitution on fractions
